entries.note: PMID 18469843 = Clement 2008 Br J Pharmacol 154:1150; quote verbatim in abstract. Peptide antagonist, product_in_model false correct. Untested stands.

Both abstracts carry the quotes verbatim (CSF ~40%; rat 'good CNS penetration'; 'translation...unproven'). CSF level in healthy volunteers is CNS exposure, not target engagement: no occupancy/PD, not patients, no source makes the comparison. Untested; merge with 2008 entry.
Osterloh 2018 abstract carries the quote verbatim. No rat exposure target vs patient exposure published; J Sex Med full texts paywalled at OUP (checked in Chrome), abstract-only. Untested stands.
Clement 2008 abstract carries the quote verbatim; model proposed for PE drug development, no patient comparison. Untested stands.

Shinghal quote verbatim; NCT01021553 results 2017-09-12, n=77, fold-diff 1.16/1.11 (p .50/.62) confirmed. Clement 2013 full text: i.v. 12 mg/kg effect 'did not reach statistical level of significance', translation 'remains to be addressed', wants CNS-penetrant antagonists. No systemic prediction; untested.

Althof quote verbatim. PEDRIX NCT03055806 results 2019-10-07, LS-mean IELT change placebo 42.6 s vs 39.7/44.5/29.2 s; PEPIX NCT02232425 results 2019-01-24, fold change 2.1 vs 1.1 (paper: ratio 1.9, P=.0079). Contra overrides same; admissible once 2013 is untested. Letter quotes unverified.

missing: Safety cell is empty but a model exists: Wayman 2018 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsxm.2018.10.008) reports >100-fold selectivity over V1A/V1B/V2 and rat dosing; Osterloh 2018 and Althof 2019 report placebo-like tolerability. No published comparison, so it could open `untested` 2018 rather than empty.

Possible earlier opening of the strip: Argiolas 1988 Eur J Pharmacol 149:389 (https://doi.org/10.1016/0014-2999(88)90675-9), a peptide OT antagonist blocking copulatory behaviour in conscious rats, cited in Clement 2013's reference list (not opened). If the conscious copulation model counts as the class's model, model_first_use_year is 1988 not 2008.

Pyke 2019 letter and the authors' reply (10.1016/j.jsxm.2019.08.010, 10.1016/j.jsxm.2019.08.023) resolve on PubMed but have no abstract; their quoted numbers (33% vs 20% placebo allocation; 43.1-second / 1.8-fold placebo response) could not be checked. Registry placebo LS-mean change 42.6 s is consistent.
rule_questions: Efficacy 2013 (epelsiban): the model's systemic arm was a non-significant trend and the authors withheld a translation claim ('remains to be addressed'); the oral trial had no engagement/exposure data. Is a null trial that never tested the model's central-OTR prediction `contra` (model wrong) or `untested` (model untested)? Brief has no engagement-confounded status; I chose untested.

Efficacy 2019 (cligosiban): same drug, same year, one positive Phase 2 (PEPIX, registry 2019-01-24) and one null, larger Phase 2b (PEDRIX, registry 2019-10-07); authors say 'The reasons for this disparity are not known.' Does contra's override apply when the patient-side evidence itself conflicts? Rules as written give contra; an 'inconclusive' status does not exist.

Engagement: is CNS exposure (CSF ~40% of unbound plasma, healthy volunteers) acceptable as engagement evidence for a CNS target when no occupancy or PD readout exists? Brief says 'hit its target in patients'; I read CSF level as exposure, not engagement, and the subjects were not patients.

Same-status entries: the brief says one entry per change of status, but the drafter's 2018 engagement/dose facts and the 2013 epelsiban null are worth keeping as facts. Is a same-status entry allowed when it carries a new fact, or must it be folded into the prior entry's note?
